cells.title: Serve five human-started bee skills from the hub with /<id> aliases
cells.action: RED FIRST in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/onboard/tests.rs, next to the existing switch tests (switching_hub, switch_fixture, the_skillstation_flag_on_a_local_project_plans_the_switch, a_fully_published_switch_leaves_no_claude_principle_folder). Give the test engine skills root a `bee-how` skill dir (SKILL.md with a frontmatter description) beside the principles. Tests: (a) the switch plan with --skillstation and runtime claude has a publish_skillstation item for bee-how, an after_publish remove_skill for bee-how (target repo-claude) and an after_publish skillstation_alias item for bee-how at .claude/skills/bee-how/SKILL.md placed after that removal, whose content carries `skillstation_alias: bee-how` and the engine description and no disable-model-invocation line; (b) apply of the full switch with every publish succeeding leaves .claude/skills/bee-how/SKILL.md as the alias, and a re-plan (hub mode, every hub-served skill active) plans no item at all for bee-how (no remove_skill, no sync, no alias); (c) a switch where the bee-how publish fails keeps the local bee-how copy and the local principles, writes no alias, and reports the skillstation-principles skipped row; (d) hub mode with the hub read failing keeps the local bee-how copy and plans no alias; (e) the codex/agents targets keep bee-how. Run them and record the red output. FIX: in skills.rs add a constant HUB_SERVED_SKILLS = [bee-how, bee-teach, bee-technical-writing, bee-why, bee-writing-skills] and a predicate (prefix PRINCIPLE_PREFIX or in the constant); use it in SkillSources::entries where without_principles filters today. In the repo-claude deletion domain loop, skip a bee-* directory when without_principles is on, the name is hub-served and its SKILL.md carries the alias marker for its own name (carries_alias_marker). In plan.rs make principle_ids return every hub-served id present in the engine skills root (principles plus the five that exist), so publish_principle_items, principles_served_by_hub and principle_removal_items cover the five. Add alias planning for the five that exist: render_alias(id, engine SKILL.md description rendered for claude, false); plan a skillstation_alias item when the repo-claude target drops them (principles_from_hub) or during the switch (marked after_publish, appended after the removals); skip the item when the current file already equals the content. In apply.rs use the predicate for the trigger flags on skill commit and for failed_principle. Principles get no alias. DOCS: scripts/install.sh --skillstation help text names the five skills and their aliases; README.md hub paragraph (the one about the 24 principles) and the --skillstation flag line say the same; docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding/skillstation-hub-skills-and-aliases.md Business Rules gain the hub-served set, the alias replacement and the deletion-domain exception citing skillstation-human-skills D1-D5 (never raw decision ids). Write docs/history/skillstation-human-skills/delivery.md (what changed, red and green test names, proof). One commit. REGEN: install.sh is a release-manifest root; finish with bee dev regen (render-skill-trees, then onboard --repo-root . --apply, then release-manifest --write) and commit the regenerated docs/history/codex-harness-hardening/release-manifest.json in the same commit.
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- skillstation onboard && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

truths: the --skillstation switch publishes, removes and aliases bee-how, bee-teach, bee-technical-writing, bee-why and bee-writing-skills for the Claude runtime
after a full switch, .claude/skills/<id>/SKILL.md for each of the five is an alias with the engine description and the re-plan plans nothing for them
a failed publish of any hub-served skill keeps every local copy and writes no alias
codex, opencode, plugin and legacy global targets keep the five

artifacts.substantive: the hub-served predicate and the deletion-domain alias exception
the hub-served ids and the alias items

key_links: every former PRINCIPLE_PREFIX test that picks the hub set calls the one predicate
aliases are rendered with render_alias and recognised with carries_alias_marker
prohibitions: Onboard tests never call the real skillstation
No new config key or CLI flag
open_choices: How the engine description is read from SKILL.md frontmatter

cells.title: Keep the /<id> alias when the --skillstation switch runs again
cells.action: DEFECT: in a project that already holds the bee-how alias at .claude/skills/bee-how/SKILL.md, a second `bee onboard --skillstation --apply` (what a re-run of scripts/install.sh --skillstation does) plans the after_publish remove_skill for bee-how from principle_removal_items, but hub_alias_items returns no item because the current file already equals the alias render. Apply deletes the alias and never writes it back; the installer recheck then plans the alias again. RED FIRST in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/onboard/tests.rs beside the shs-1 tests: run the full switch apply with every publish succeeding, then run a second switch apply with the hub now reporting every hub-served skill active with the same files; assert .claude/skills/bee-how/SKILL.md still exists and carries `skillstation_alias: bee-how`, and that a plan without --skillstation (hub mode, all served) plans no item naming bee-how. Watch it fail for the reported reason and record the red output. FIX in plan.rs, smallest change: during the switch (after_publish true) hub_alias_items always plans the alias item, because the removal before it deletes the folder; the equal-content skip stays only for the non-switch path. Add one sentence to the Business Rules of docs/knowledge/areas/onboarding/skillstation-hub-skills-and-aliases.md that a re-run of the switch rewrites the alias after the removal, citing skillstation-human-skills D3-D4. Add the red and green test names to docs/history/skillstation-human-skills/delivery.md. One commit.
cells.verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --bin bee -- skillstation onboard

truths: a second --skillstation apply on a project that already holds the five aliases leaves every alias in place
after that second apply, a plan without --skillstation plans no item for the five

artifacts.substantive: the switch alias items are planned even when the file is current

key_links: the alias item still sorts after the remove_skill item for the same id
prohibitions: Onboard tests never call the real skillstation
